review: 1:2 מְחַיֶּה בִּרְכוֹתָיו — 'who gives life to His blessings', for مُحْيِي تَهَانِيهَا; the Arabic ثَنَايَا/تَهَانِي is congratulations, which has no biblical noun, so בְּרָכוֹת carries it.
2:2 תִּזְרַח — יָאִיר שַׁחֲרִי — the dash marks the caesura the Arabic has (لُحْتَ / ابْتَدَا); the verb זָרַח is the psalm verb for dawn (Ps 112:4).
3:3–3:4 אֶרְאֶה לְבָבוֹ כְּמוֹ / יִרְאֶה הוּא לְלִבִּי — 'I see His heart as He sees my heart'; the reciprocity is the Arabic's point and is kept, with the infinitive-like balance of the two lines.
4:1–4:3 תַּחְפֹּץ ... לַעֲזֹב ... וְלַעֲלוֹת — a chain of infinitives after a finite verb; the Arabic switches from أَنْ تَتْرُكَ to وَتَرْتَقِي, and Hebrew keeps the chain to hold the line lengths.
